FORTIS INC. RELEASES THIRD QUARTER 
2026 
RESULTS, NEW FIVE-YEAR CAPITAL OUTLOOK AND 4% INCREASE IN FOURTH QUARTER DIVIDEND
This news release constitutes a "Designated News Release" incorporated by reference in the prospectus supplement 
dated December 9, 2024 to Fortis' short form base shelf prospectus dated December 9, 2024.
Fortis Inc. ("Fortis" or the "Corporation") (TSX/NYSE: FTS), a diversified leader in the North American regulated electric and gas utility industry, released its third quarter results and 2027-2031 outlook.
1
Highlights 
•
Third quarter net earnings of $474 million or $0.92 per common share, up from $0.81 per common share in 2025
•
Adjusted net earnings per common share
2
 of $0.92, up from $0.87 per common share in the third quarter of 2025
•
Capital expenditures
2
 of $4.2 billion through September; capital investment of $6.0 billion expected for 2026
•
Released 2027-2031 capital plan of $32.2 billion, $3.4 billion higher than prior plan and supporting 7.5% rate base growth
3
•
Competitive project in Iowa totalling US$1.0 billion awarded to ITC, with US$0.5 billion reflected in the new five-year plan
•
Environmental approval received for both the Tilbury LNG Storage Tank and Phase 2 LNG Expansion projects in British Columbia
•
Recommended Opinion and Order issued with respect to TEP's rate application 
•
Increased fourth quarter common share dividend by 4% and extended annual dividend growth guidance of 4-6% through 2031
"During the third quarter, our utilities executed key capital investments while advancing strategic growth initiatives across our portfolio, including a competitive transmission project at ITC and the Tilbury 1B and Phase 2 LNG expansion projects at FortisBC," said David Hutchens, President and Chief Executive Officer, Fortis. "Today, we are introducing our new $32.2 billion five-year capital plan, the largest in Fortis history, which reflects the critical investments required to deliver safe, reliable and resilient energy service to our customers. With a strong pipeline of regulated investment opportunities and a proven track record of execution, we are well positioned to deliver sustained rate base growth and 4-6% annual dividend growth through 2031."
Net Earnings 
The Corporation reported net earnings attributable to common equity shareholders ("Net Earnings") of $474 million for the third quarter of 2026, or $0.92 per common share, an increase of $65 million, or $0.11 per common share compared to the third quarter of 2025. The disposition of FortisTCI in September 2025 resulted in the recognition of income taxes and closing costs of $32 million, or $0.06 per common share, in the third quarter of 2025. Excluding this impact, Net Earnings increased by $33 million quarter-over-quarter primarily due to rate base growth across our utilities. The increase was also due to higher earnings at UNS Energy, reflecting growth in retail electricity sales and the timing of operating costs, partially offset by costs associated with rate base growth not yet reflected in customer rates. The 2025 dispositions of FortisTCI and Fortis Belize and higher holding company finance costs also unfavourably impacted earnings growth for the quarter.
On a year-to-date basis, excluding the impact of income taxes and closing costs related to the 2025 disposition of FortisTCI discussed above, Net Earnings increased by $47 million, or $0.06 per common share. The increase was primarily driven by rate base growth across our utilities, as well as the timing of costs at Central Hudson. These impacts were partially offset by lower earnings at UNS Energy due to lower margin on wholesale sales and costs associated with rate base growth not yet reflected in customer rates, partially offset by higher retail electricity sales. The dispositions of FortisTCI and Fortis Belize in 2025, higher holding company finance costs, and a lower foreign exchange rate also moderated year-to-date earnings growth.
The change in earnings per common share for both the third quarter and year-to-date periods also reflected an increase in the weighted average number of common shares outstanding associated with the Corporation's dividend reinvestment and at-the-market ("ATM") equity plans.
On an adjusted earnings per common share basis, the 2025 dispositions had a $0.02 and $0.05 dilutive impact on third quarter and year-to-date results, respectively.

Adjusted Net Earnings
2

Adjusted net earnings attributable to common equity shareholders ("Adjusted Net Earnings") reflects the removal of items that management excludes in its key decision-making processes and evaluation of operating results. There were no adjustments to Net Earnings for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, Net Earnings were favourably adjusted by $32 million related to the disposition of FortisTCI, as previously discussed.
2026 Capital Expenditures and New Five-Year Capital Plan
Capital expenditures for 2026 are expected to be approximately $6.0 billion, up from $5.6 billion previously anticipated for the year. The increase is largely driven by the acceleration of major capital projects, including tranche 1 Midcontinent Independent System Operator ("MISO") long-range transmission plan ("LRTP") investments at ITC, and the Tilbury Phase 1B project at FortisBC Energy. 
The Corporation's new 2027-2031 capital plan totals $32.2 billion, $3.4 billion higher than the previous five-year plan. The increase is primarily driven by FERC-regulated transmission investments at ITC related to the MISO LRTP tranche 2.1 portfolio of projects, including a competitive project in Iowa awarded to ITC in October 2026, as well as ongoing investment in system reliability and interconnections. The increase also reflects continued development of the Tilbury site, including the Phase 1B expansion and the Liquefied Natural Gas ("LNG") Storage Tank projects at FortisBC Energy, as well as customer growth and reliability-related investments across the Corporation's utilities. The plan is low-risk and highly executable.
The five-year capital plan is expected to be funded primarily by cash from operations and regulated utility debt. Common equity is expected to be predominantly supported by the Corporation's dividend reinvestment plan. The Corporation advanced a portion of its equity funding requirements through the issuance of US$1.0 billion of junior subordinated notes and approximately $260 million of common shares through the ATM equity program in the third quarter of 2026. The Corporation intends to file a new short-form base shelf prospectus and re-establish the ATM equity program in early 2027 to provide funding flexibility. 
Significant opportunities remain beyond the five-year plan, including incremental investments associated with MISO LRTP tranche 2.1 projects. ITC estimates a range of US$2.9 billion to US$3.4 billion in capital expenditures beyond the new five-year capital plan for MISO tranche 2.1 projects located in Michigan and Minnesota, where rights of first refusal are in effect, and for projects requiring system upgrades in Iowa which are not subject to a competitive bidding process. In addition, a competitive project in Iowa of US$1.0 billion was recently awarded to ITC, of which US$0.5 billion is included in the five-year plan.
In September 2026, FortisBC Energy received an Environmental Assessment Certificate from the Province of British Columbia and the Government of Canada for the Tilbury Phase 2 LNG Expansion which would provide up to 2.5 million tonnes per annum to serve emerging LNG markets, including marine fuelling. No capital has been included in our new five-year plan associated with the Phase 2 liquefaction expansion project, but investment opportunity of $2 billion to $4 billion exists, depending on market use and a final investment decision. The majority of this investment is expected beyond 2031.
UNS Energy is experiencing strong interest from new and existing customers associated with economic development activity, including opportunities related to data centers, mining, industrial development, electrification, and broader commercial and residential growth. These opportunities could drive additional investment in generation, transmission, and distribution infrastructure over time. Tucson Electric Power ("TEP") and UNS Electric filed new Integrated Resource Plans ("IRPs") in October 2026 that support customers' projected energy needs over the next 15 years while maintaining reliability and affordability. The base case IRPs reflect opportunity above the five-year plan of up to US$1.6 billion through 2031, subject to request for proposal processes. To evaluate the potential growth above the base case IRP, TEP included a high-load factor scenario in its IRP that assumes approximately 800 MW of additional generation and could require up to US$1.5 billion of incremental investment. These opportunities are not currently reflected in the Corporation's five-year capital plan but represent meaningful long-term growth potential for the business.
Regulatory Update
In October 2026, an Arizona Corporation Commission ("ACC") Administrative Law Judge issued a Recommended Opinion and Order with respect to TEP's general rate application, recommending an allowed rate of return on common equity of 9.65% and a 55.5% common equity component of capital structure. The order also included an annual formulaic rate adjustment mechanism with a range of +/‑ 50 basis points around the allowed ROE, the inclusion of post-test year adjustments, and the deferral of certain costs associated with owning and operating the Roadrunner Reserve II battery storage project for future recovery. The Recommended Opinion and Order proposes implementation of new rates by December 1, 2026. The rate application remains subject to ACC approval which is anticipated later this month.
ii
Fourth Quarter 2026 Dividends 
The Board of Directors of Fortis has declared the following dividends payable on December 1, 2026 to the Shareholders of Record of the following Shares of the Corporation at the close of business on November 17, 2026:
•
$0.3063 per share on the First Preference Shares, Series "F";
•
$0.3826875 per share on the First Preference Shares, Series "G";
•
$0.26144 per share on the First Preference Shares, Series "H";
•
$0.23311 per share on the First Preference Shares, Series "I";
•
$0.2969 per share on the First Preference Shares, Series "J";
•
$0.3418125 per share on the First Preference Shares, Series "K";
•
$0.3433125 per share on the First Preference Shares, Series "M"; and,
•
$0.665 per share on the Common Shares.
The Corporation has designated the common share dividend and preference share dividends as eligible dividends for federal and provincial dividend tax credit purposes. 
Outlook
Fortis continues to enhance shareholder value through the execution of its capital plan, the balance and strength of its diversified portfolio of regulated utility businesses, and growth opportunities within and proximate to its service territories. The Corporation's $32.2 billion five-year capital plan is expected to increase midyear rate base from $45.3 billion in 2026 to $55.8 billion by 2029 and $63.9 billion by 2031, translating into three- and five-year compound annual growth rates of 7.7% and 7.5%, respectively.

Fortis expects its long-term growth in rate base will drive earnings that support dividend growth guidance of 4-6% annually through 2031.
Above and beyond the five-year capital plan, growth opportunities include: further expansion of the electric transmission grid in the U.S. to support load growth and facilitate the interconnection of new energy resources, including transmission investments associated with the MISO LRTP and MISO transmission expansion plan; grid resiliency and climate adaptation investments; investments in renewable gas and LNG infrastructure in British Columbia; and energy infrastructure investments to support the acceleration of load growth across our jurisdictions.

DESCRIPTION OF BUSINESS
Nature of Operations
Fortis Inc. ("Fortis" or the "Corporation") is a diversified North American regulated electric and gas utility holding company.
Earnings for interim periods may not be indicative of annual results due to: (i) the impact of seasonal weather conditions on customer demand; (ii) the impact of market conditions, particularly with respect to long-term wholesale sales at UNS Energy; (iii) the timing and significance of any regulatory decisions; and (iv) changes in the U.S. dollar-to-Canadian dollar exchange rate. Earnings for the utilities in Canada and New York tend to be highest in the first and fourth quarters due to space-heating requirements. Earnings for UNS Energy tend to be highest in the second and third quarters due to the use of air conditioning and other cooling equipment.
Entities within the reporting segments that follow operate with substantial autonomy.

2. REGULATORY MATTERS
Regulation of the Corporation's utilities is generally consistent with that disclosed in Note 2 of the Corporation's annual audited consolidated financial statements ("2025 Annual Financial Statements"). A summary of significant outstanding regulatory matters follows.
ITC
Transmission Incentives: 
In 2021, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission ("FERC") issued a supplemental notice of proposed rulemaking ("NOPR") on transmission incentives modifying the proposal in the initial NOPR released by FERC in 2020. The supplemental NOPR proposes to eliminate the 50-basis point regional transmission organization ("RTO") return on common equity ("ROE") incentive adder for RTO members that have been members for longer than three years. The timing and outcome of this proceeding are unknown.
UNS Energy
TEP General Rate Application: 
In October 2026, an Arizona Corporation Commission ("ACC") Administrative Law Judge issued a Recommended Opinion and Order with respect to TEP's rate application, recommending an allowed ROE of 9.65% and a 55.5% common equity component of capital structure. The order also included an annual formulaic rate adjustment mechanism with a range of +/- 50 basis points around the allowed ROE, the inclusion of post-test year adjustments, the elimination of certain adjustor mechanisms, and the deferral of certain costs associated with owning and operating the Roadrunner Reserve II battery storage project for future recovery. The Recommended Opinion and Order proposes implementation of new rates by December 1, 2026. The rate application remains subject to ACC approval which is anticipated in November 2026.
The ACC approved a formula rate policy statement in 2024. The Residential Utility Consumer Office has challenged the ACC's authority to implement a formula rate framework through a policy statement, and in November 2025, the Arizona Court of Appeals ruled that the Residential Utility Consumer Office may proceed with its challenge. The timing and outcome of these regulatory and legal proceedings are unknown. The ACC has previously approved adjustor mechanisms, including formula-based mechanisms, in rate cases.

A decision from the AUC is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. No impact to earnings is anticipated as the related updates to revenue and depreciation expense are expected to be neutral.

14. FAIR VALUE OF FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS AND RISK MANAGEMENT 
Derivatives
The Corporation generally limits the use of derivatives to those that qualify as accounting, economic or cash flow hedges, or those that are approved for regulatory recovery. 
Derivatives are recorded at fair value with certain exceptions including those derivatives that qualify for the normal purchase and normal sale exception. Fair values reflect estimates based on current market information about the derivatives as at the balance sheet dates. The estimates cannot be determined with precision as they involve uncertainties and matters of judgment and, therefore, may not be relevant in predicting the Corporation's future consolidated earnings or cash flow.
Energy Contracts Subject to Regulatory Deferral
UNS Energy holds electricity power purchase contracts, gas supply contracts and gas swap contracts to reduce its exposure to energy price risk. Fair values are measured primarily under the market approach using independent third-party information, where possible. When published prices are not available, adjustments are applied based on historical price curve relationships, transmission costs and line losses.
Central Hudson holds swap contracts for electricity and natural gas to minimize price volatility by fixing the effective purchase price. Fair values are measured using forward pricing provided by independent third-party information.
FortisBC Energy holds gas supply contracts to fix the effective purchase price of natural gas. Fair values reflect the present value of future cash flows based on published market prices and forward natural gas price curves. 
Unrealized gains or losses associated with changes in the fair value of these energy contracts are deferred as a regulatory asset or liability for recovery from, or refund to, customers in future rates, as permitted by the regulators. As at September 30, 2026, unrealized losses of $112 million (December 31, 2025 - $135 million) were recognized as regulatory assets and unrealized gains of $21 million (December 31, 2025 - $37 million) were recognized as regulatory liabilities.

Credit Risk
For cash equivalents, accounts receivable and other current assets, and long-term other receivables, credit risk is generally limited to the carrying value on the consolidated balance sheets. The Corporation's subsidiaries generally have a large and diversified customer base, which minimizes the concentration of credit risk. Policies in place to minimize credit risk include requiring customer deposits, prepayments and/or credit checks for certain customers, performing disconnections and/or using third-party collection agencies for overdue accounts.
ITC has a concentration of credit risk as approximately 70% of its revenue is derived from three customers. The customers have investment-grade credit ratings and credit risk is further managed by the Midcontinent Independent System Operator by requiring a letter of credit or cash deposit equal to the credit exposure, which is determined by a credit-scoring model and other factors.
FortisAlberta has a concentration of credit risk as its distribution service billings are to a relatively small group of retailers. Credit risk is managed by obtaining from the retailers either a cash deposit, letter of credit, an investment-grade credit rating, or a financial guarantee from an entity with an investment-grade credit rating.
Central Hudson has seen an increase in accounts receivable since the suspension of collection efforts initially required in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Central Hudson continues to contact customers regarding past-due balances and collection efforts are ongoing. Under its regulatory framework, Central Hudson can defer uncollectible write-offs above the amounts collected in customer rates for future recovery.
ITC, UNS Energy, Central Hudson, FortisBC Energy, and Fortis may be exposed to credit risk in the event of non-performance by counterparties to derivative contracts. Credit risk is managed by net settling payments, when possible, and dealing only with counterparties that have investment-grade credit ratings. At UNS Energy, Central Hudson and FortisBC Energy, certain contractual arrangements require counterparties to post collateral.

TEP General Rate Application:

The order also included an annual formulaic rate adjustment mechanism with a range of +/- 50 basis points around the allowed ROE, the inclusion of post-test year adjustments, the elimination of certain adjustor mechanisms, and the deferral of certain costs associated with owning and operating the Roadrunner Reserve II battery storage project for future recovery. The subsidiaries pay dividends to Fortis and receive equity injections from Fortis when required. Both Fortis and its subsidiaries initially borrow through their credit facilities and periodically replace these borrowings with long-term financing.
